### 1. Difference between Unit Operation and Unit Process

| Feature | Unit Operation | Unit Process |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Basis** | Physical changes (transfer of momentum, heat, or mass) | Chemical changes (involving chemical reactions) |
| **Governing Laws** | Principles of momentum, heat, and mass transfer | Chemical thermodynamics and reaction kinetics |
| **Example** | Distillation, Filtration, Evaporation, Drying | Oxidation, Hydrogenation, Polymerization, Sulfonation |

### 2. Role and Responsibilities of a Chemical Engineer
* **Process Design & Development:** Designing safe, efficient, and cost-effective chemical manufacturing processes from laboratory scale to industrial scale (Scale-up).
* **Plant Operations & Troubleshooting:** Monitoring continuous plant operations, optimizing parameters (temperature, pressure, flow rates), and resolving equipment malfunctions.
* **Safety and Environmental Compliance:** Ensuring compliance with OSHA, EPA, and local environmental standards; managing hazardous waste and preventing process safety accidents.
* **Economics & Project Management:** Estimating capital and operating costs, managing budgets, and selecting construction materials.
